Full-thickness burns: 2

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A deeply burned area is less painful than adjacent red blistered skin. Which principle prevents the examiner from incorrectly concluding that the less painful center is necessarily the less severe part of the injury?

  1. Include partial- and full-thickness areas in TBSA
  2. Cool the burn safely and assess severity
  3. Re-epithelialization from preserved viable epidermal sources
  4. Pain intensity does not reliably measure burn depth
  5. Exclude purely superficial burns from resuscitation TBSA
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Pain intensity does not reliably measure burn depth

Destruction of sensory endings can make a deeper area less painful than a superficial one.

Understanding the options

Pain intensity does not reliably measure burn depth
Destruction of sensory endings can make a deeper area less painful than a superficial one.
Exclude purely superficial burns from resuscitation TBSA
Burn-area estimates used for major burn assessment count partial- and full-thickness injury, not simple superficial erythema. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Include partial- and full-thickness areas in TBSA
Dermal and deeper burns contribute to the burn area used for severity and resuscitation assessment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Cool the burn safely and assess severity
Appropriate cool running water first aid and protection are used; ice and additional cold injury should be avoided. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Re-epithelialization from preserved viable epidermal sources
Superficial injuries retain capacity for epithelial regeneration; deeper loss reduces this reserve. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
